text:
Jordan: FYI ACME just escalated — their streaming requests are getting billed as 5xx even though client sees a broken pipe. request_id=abc123def tenant=acme-prod :frowning:

Tara: Ugh. Do we have the raw gateway logs and the customer's client-side stacktrace? :eyes:

Jordan: I pulled the gateway trace:
```
2026-03-17T16:10:05Z gateway[worker-7]: conn_id=gw-11ff request_id=abc123def upstream_status=RST_STREAM reason=connection_reset_by_peer
2026-03-17T16:10:05Z gateway[worker-7]: tokens_charged=12 error_classification=5xx
```
Customer says their client closed socket after receiving final chunks. They claim they were billed for 12 tokens which they think is wrong.

Mike: That log looks like our proxy observed a reset (RST) while streaming and classified as 5xx. We have a heuristic that marks upstream RST without trailer as 5xx. If the client did a half-close / FIN after consuming chunks we should treat as client_abort not gateway_error.

Lee: Can you reproduce quickly? Most of the time this is an interleaving of chunked trailers vs FIN detection. Small race where proxy sees RST from client while upstream still writing a trailer.

Jordan: Repro steps from customer (copied):
1) Open streaming connection to /v1/streams with Transfer-Encoding: chunked
2) Receive several chunk frames, then client application calls close() immediately after last chunk
3) We sometimes observe server writing chunk-trailer and then socket RSTs.

Tara: Can you try a simple repro script? I used this raw-socket python snippet to force early close and reproduce locally: 
```
# python repro_close.py
import socket, time
s = socket.create_connection(('api.redwood-inference.com', 443))
# TLS omitted in snippet for brevity; reproduce via tcp proxy
s.send(b"POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n")
s.send(b"4\r\ntest\r\n0\r\n\r\n")
# close immediately to simulate client-side FIN
s.close()
```
I can hit the gateway and usually trigger the RST path. :thumbsup:

Mike: Ok that reproduces. Telemetry shows our conn-metrics: upstream wrote trailer, then within 10ms we saw client-side FIN followed by proxy observed ECONNRESET. Current classifier marks this as gateway_error because trailer didn't flush before reset.

support-bot: Billing note: our billing pipeline treats gateway-classified 5xx as billable by default. If we determine it was client-initiated abort, we can issue an automated credit. Please open an account-level dispute if ACME wants immediate credit.

Lee: Proposed fix: modify gateway to detect "trailer_written && client_fin_seen" and mark as client_abort instead of 5xx. Also add a 50ms grace window for trailer flush before final classification. Low-risk change but needs careful e2e tests.

Jordan: Who owns the patch? This is affecting a paying customer.

Lee: I will own the change. I'll open a P1 issue and a small changelist for the classifier. Will add unit + integration tests.

Tara: For now, tell ACME workaround: slight delay between sending last chunk and socket close (50-100ms) or upgrade client to wait for TCP close/ACK. Also we can offer temporary credit if they want.

Jordan: Thanks — I'll reply to the customer with repro steps, the workaround, and offer provisional credit. I'll file the billing dispute link and attach request_id=abc123def.

Mike: I'll add observability: pulse metric for "trailer_vs_fin_race" and alert if > 0.1% of streams hit this path.

infra-bot: Deploy patch branch available in staging: refs/changes/CL-7890, test matrix queued.

Jordan: Great. Tagging @Tara @Lee @Mike. Closing here once CL lands and customer notified. :white_check_mark:
